<!-- pr-reviewer: d9676f812b06ab69049678a4a5dcf416190863a7 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

**What looks good**
- Banded streaming runs the same `judge_rows` body as the whole-lattice pass. Rows ascend and the best is replaced only on a strict `>`, so the first worst wins, as in the single pass. In `banded`, the per-row claim counts use the same `plane_claim` calls as the binning, so a band's held claims equal its counted claims.
- Band edges: a facet is active in a band when `j0 < jb && j1 >= ja`, and each band clips its rows to `(j0.max(ja), j1.min(jb-1))`. A column or facet straddling two bands is claimed exactly once per row, in the band that owns that row.
- Bin claim order differs between the single pass and the bands (facets are visited sorted by first row). `crossings_from_claims` sorts by `z` with `total_cmp`, so only claims with equal `z` can reorder. Those sum identically, and the pairing groups use a tolerance, so the verdict does not change.
- Refusals: `rows_cap == 0`, a single row over `claims`, and the `work` cap all return `OverBudget` by name, never a zero. Progress is guaranteed: the first row of every band is already checked to fit.
- `scan_near.rs` is exact. Segments are indexed in every cell a piece (at most one cell long) touches. The ring walk breaks only when `(k-1)*g` combined with the Z gap reaches the best distance found. Rings outside the grid are skipped, which also bounds the loop. The early exit returns an upper bound that is at or under the worst rest, so it can never raise the answer.
- `ScanBudget` is used only inside camcraft-sim (`scan.rs`, `stock_sim` tests, the new suite). I found no caller in app, ui or motion, so the new public `work` field breaks nothing.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` in the new code. Indexing uses `get` or is range-bounded. Both new files carry a provenance line. The decision record is in `docs/decisions/24-field-scan-verdict.md`. The body ends `Fixes #24` and has a `Changelog:` line.

**Local results** (trial merge with current origin/main was clean; no build.rs, `.github`, script or dependency changes)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`, all suites incl. `hidden_rest_banded` (5 pass, 1 ignored heavy lane) and `stock_sim` (55 pass, incl. `hidden_rest_over_budget_says_not_judged`) | all ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| camcraft-app `posed_contact` | 5 pass |
| camcraft-app `turning_form` | 8 pass |
| camcraft-app `turning_thread` | 8 pass |
| camcraft-app `verify` | 21 pass, 2 ignored |
| motion `finish3d` | not run (slow; the author reports green) |

Adversarial check, written locally and not committed: a thin ledge box (0.05 to 0.7 mm wide) swept across 40 y/x offsets, so edges fall on and between band boundaries, under 6 tight claim and cell budgets each. All 200 streamed verdicts that were not refused were bit-identical to the whole scan in `rest_mm` and in the location `at`.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The whole-lattice attempt runs first and can build up to 40 M claims (~1.6 GB) before it falls back to the bands, so the shipped 21-plate case pays that cost once. Counting claims before the first pass would save it; this is only a time cost.
2. The grid indexes interpolated piece endpoints. A segment point can sit about 1e-16 mm across a cell edge from its indexed cell, which is far below the 0.1 mm floor and has no effect on the verdict.
3. `crates/sim/tests/stock_sim.rs` was already over 400 lines and grows slightly. `scan.rs` (431) is unchanged. Neither blocks the merge.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
